title: Semantic space: two retrievals with the same meaning

events.label: Three documents ready
events.detail: ① Return policy: items may be returned within 30 days of delivery ② Refund process: 3–5 business days back to the original payment method after review ③ Invoicing: electronic and paper invoices supported.

events.label: Documents embedded
events.detail: Each passage is mapped to a 1024-dimension vector — the embedding model encodes 'meaning' as geometry: the closer the semantics, the smaller the angle between vectors.

events.label: Vectors stored
events.detail: Vectors are written into the store with their text and metadata (section, update date). The model used at indexing time is frozen from that moment.

events.label: First query: original wording
events.detail: "What is the return policy?" — nearly identical to document ① on the surface.

events.label: Nearest-neighbor search
events.detail: The query is embedded too, ranked by cosine similarity, top-3 taken — cosine is the norm for text over Euclidean distance: it compares direction, not length.

events.label: First hit list
events.detail: Return policy 0.91 / refund process 0.87 / invoicing 0.42 — the first two share the 'returns' semantic cluster; invoicing trails at the bottom.

events.label: Second query: a paraphrase
events.detail: "I bought the wrong thing — can I send it back?" — almost zero lexical overlap with the documents; this tests semantics.

events.label: Nearest-neighbor search (second)
events.detail: Same vectors, same ranking; only the query text changed.

events.label: Second hit list compared
events.detail: Return policy 0.88 / refund process 0.83 / invoicing 0.40 — different wording, same meaning, both still hit. That is the point of embeddings: close in meaning despite different characters.

events.label: A miss case
events.detail: Query 'warranty terms' — no such document exists in the store, and the top-1 similarity is only 0.31. Below threshold, return 'not found'; forcing the nearest neighbor is more dangerous than an empty result.

events.label: Dimensions and selection discipline
events.detail: 1024 dimensions is a selection outcome: higher dimensions mean more expressiveness and higher storage and search costs. Once chosen, the embedding model is frozen — switching models means re-embedding the whole store (chunks in R03 too), which is why selection deserves deliberation.

events.label: Approximate nearest neighbors (ANN)
events.detail: Exact nearest neighbors cannot scan billions of vectors; ANN indexes trade a little recall for millisecond latency. How much recall is lost is an evaluation question — R05's metrics are the ruler.
